critical_code_review_comments: public_submit re-uses resolve_token(payload.token) which raises 404/410 on inactive/expired — good pattern (single source of truth). But note the fetched envelope's 'already_submitted' is read from the invite doc as it existed BEFORE the submit, so the duplicate-invite guard is race-safe only if invites collection has a unique index on token — currently there is no explicit index. Consider adding db.player_registration_invites.create_index('token', unique=True) on startup (defense in depth).

approve_registration builds player_id via count_documents on (body_id, season_year) — under concurrent approvals this can yield duplicate player_ids because count is not atomic. Prefer $inc on a counters collection or a Mongo transaction. Low likelihood but flag it.

_may_read fallback for districts is a 'best-effort' string check (body_code.startswith('DIST-') AND campaign body_code.startswith('DIV-')) — this lets ANY district read ANY division's campaign, not just its own parent. Comment in code already acknowledges this — worth a follow-up fix once bodies hierarchy is available. Not currently exposed in UI.

PublicPlayerRegistration uploads route hits POST /api/uploads without auth headers — /api/uploads currently requires auth in this app; if a public applicant tries to attach a photo/aadhaar, upload may 401 or 403. Not exercised in acceptance tests but users could hit it. Verify /api/uploads accepts anonymous uploads for related_type='player_registration' or use a signed public endpoint.

PlayerRegistrations.jsx: NewCampaignDialog defaults body_code to persona.body_code || 'MPCA'. When a Division opens the dialog then edits body_code to another value (e.g. MPCA), BE returns 403; the form surfaces the raw detail — good — but disabling/read-only would be a cleaner UX for Division personas.
